title: Windows VM: create launcher after start; clear setgid on harden
head: 799827f4dec9
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Empty shared directory can become world-readable and world-writable again after VM startup, including through its traversable protected bind anchor
leads.consequence: When Dockur can write an initially empty /shared, samba.sh chmods it to 2777 after the pre-start 700 hardening. The same inode is exposed at /var/lib/omarchy/windows/mounts/users/<uid>/shared, whose ancestors the root helper sets to 0755/0711/0711/0711. On a normally traversable /var/lib tree, another local account can traverse that anchor, list the share, create or remove entries and access any files whose individual modes permit it (Dockur config specifies `force create mode = 0666` at src/samba.sh:239), despite a private HOME. The install path does not reharden after dc up -d, and stop only invokes dc down, so the exposure can persist until a subsequent privileged up/remove or reboot. This vulnerability predates the PR; changing the chmod spelling repairs subsequent operations but does not establish ongoing privacy. Consider restoring exact 0700 after Dockur's initialization and on stop without losing the anchored inode, as #9783 separately attempts.

leads.summary: New removal regression passes when root removal stops re-hardening the setgid share
leads.consequence: The test applies chmod 2777 and then calls prepare_caller_mounts itself at :455, before __priv_remove. The real root removal path depends on assert_mounts_safe calling that helper at bin/omarchy-windows-vm:889-891. In the test's non-root development namespace, this root-only branch does not run. Deleting that root-side call is a plausible regression that would leave a 2777 shared anchor, fail mounts_ready before deleting the disk, and make user-side remove exit 1 while leaving the launcher and VM data. Yet the new test still passes because it has already repaired the mode. Exercise root removal directly after chmod 2777 without an explicit helper call, using the existing isolated root boundary fixture.
leads.triage: corroborated; matches Opus mutant P; published in test notes

leads.summary: Launcher write failure is ignored after the VM has started, so install reports success with no Remove menu entry
leads.consequence: If ~/.local/share/applications is not creatable or the entry cannot be written, create_launcher_entry fails but install_windows runs later echo/xdg-open commands and can exit 0. The VM and credentials/compose remain, while menu Remove > Windows is hidden and Install stays available because both guards test for the desktop file. Retry may overwrite configuration and prompt to install again; CLI remove remains available. This unchecked writer also existed before relocation, so it is a surviving boundary defect rather than a newly introduced regression. Propagate a launcher-write error or make installed-state detection independent of this optional file.
leads.triage: verified_not_published; unchecked create_launcher_entry, no set -e; pre-existing edge case, low value

leads.summary: Related open VM fixes collide with this head; preserve strict privacy and protected compose during manual conflict resolution
leads.consequence: All related heads examined diverge from this PR. Three-way merging #10113 conflicts at the chmod block but independently imports checks accepting every mode with owner rwx, including 2777, into mounted_leaf_matches and the post-chmod validation. Resolving only the visible chmod conflict while keeping those checks would undermine this PR's exact-700 guard if Dockur or a concurrent writer reapplies 2777. #4882 conflicts in the compose writer; taking its old branch would revert the protected root-owned compose to a user-owned compose with direct HOME binds, a security regression. #10262 conflicts at the same procfd chmod line; retain symbolic hardening while incorporating its BASHPID snapshot. #9783's post-start privacy watcher is not redundant and conflicts in both chmod sites. The exact-mode alternatives #12323, #13213, #12019, #13154, #10411, #9605, #10338, #12155 and #10962 also conflict in chmod sites; #8796 and #7144 conflict in the RDP argument block. This is a manual integration hazard, not a claim that an automatic merger silently weakens the code.
leads.triage: partly_verified; #9783 overlap verified via gh api and published neutrally; other PR conflicts are merge hazards, not published

leads.summary: New launcher ordering test passes even when the install call is unreachable
leads.consequence: The test checks source line numbers and executes only an extracted create_launcher_entry function, not install_windows. A plausible inverted guard requiring the applications directory to be absent that leaves the exact text `  create_launcher_entry` after priv up makes all three assertions pass, yet installations where the applications directory already exists never get their marker and the Remove menu item remains hidden. A mocked interactive install that calls install_windows and checks both successful up and failed up paths would catch this.
leads.triage: dropped; launcher test mutant gap; low value, F3 accurate as stated

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12264#issuecomment-5833657119), checked on head `799827f4` (rebased onto `d201fb95`), including the [removal reproduction report](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12264#issuecomment-5835518124) and the regression test pulled in from it.

**Verified:** no behavior defect was found in the tested scope. The rebase changed nothing in `bin/omarchy-windows-vm`, and the only script change since the earlier review is the dropped `mkdir`.

```text
Earlier finding                               Status on 799827f4
--------------------------------------------  ---------------------------------------
Launcher entry written only after priv up     still verified, unchanged
Setgid cleared when hardening directories     still verified, trigger now confirmed
New launcher test                             still verified, test file unchanged
Re-added mkdir -p "$HOME/.windows"            resolved (b5d6270 removes it)
Optional: no test for the setgid change       partly resolved (root side only)
```

### Setgid fix: Dockur supplies the trigger

**Verified** in Dockur source ([`src/samba.sh` L154-160](https://github.com/dockur/windows/blob/1e99833c8f7946238566ecd0d5d2b40ba5f6c03a/src/samba.sh#L154-L160)): when the shared directory is empty and writable, each container start that reaches Dockur's Samba setup (after the image download on a first install) runs `chmod 2777` on it. That has been `2777` since Dockur v5.08; earlier releases used `777`, which the base's `chmod 0700` handled. On the base, the next privileged `prepare_caller_mounts` (launch or remove) leaves `2700`, fails the exact-`700` check and returns 1, so removal stops with the generic "stopped before user-side cleanup" error. On the head the same step yields `700` and continues. This matches the reproduction report; the installed 4.0.4-1 package itself was not inspected.

```text
start mode   chmod 0700 (base)   chmod a-s,u=rwx,go= (head)
----------   -----------------   --------------------------
755          700                 700
2777         2700                700
6777         6700                700
```

### New removal regression test

**Verified:** in `windows-vm-compose-test.sh`, the test passes on the head (22 `ok`) and fails on the base script (exit 1). It also fails when only the root-side `chmod` ([L585](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/799827f4dec959c33068aa4ce26b82ffd102fd00/bin/omarchy-windows-vm#L585)) is reverted to `chmod 0700`. That covers the root side of the earlier optional test note. Reverting only the user-side `chmod` ([L1020](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/799827f4dec959c33068aa4ce26b82ffd102fd00/bin/omarchy-windows-vm#L1020)) still passes, so that line remains uncovered; both callers go on to the privileged step, which re-hardens.

The test runs as non-root, and [`assert_mounts_safe`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/799827f4dec959c33068aa4ce26b82ffd102fd00/bin/omarchy-windows-vm#L889-L891) calls `prepare_caller_mounts` only when `EUID == 0`. The explicit `prepare_caller_mounts` call in the test is therefore what clears the bit, as its comment says. Consequences:

- Deleting that root-branch call from `assert_mounts_safe` still passes the test, so the production link from removal to hardening is not exercised.
- The final assertion's message, "removal left the shared directory setgid", credits removal with the helper's work.
- On the base, the run aborts through `set -e` with no `not ok` line naming the cause.

**Optional test improvement:** assert the setup, gate the helper and reword the final assertion message, so the base reports a named failure (not run as written):

```bash
chmod 2777 "$HOME/Windows"
[[ $(stat -c '%a' "$HOME/Windows") == 2777 ]] || fail "test setup made the shared directory setgid"
prepare_caller_mounts || fail "prepare_caller_mounts hardens a setgid shared directory"
```

`windows-vm-mount-boundary-test.sh` already runs as `EUID == 0` in a user namespace. Setting its shared target to `2777` before `with_vm_lock assert_mounts_safe` and asserting `700` afterwards would cover the root-only link (source-traced, not run: it needs subordinate IDs).

### Shared directory reopens after each start (pre-existing, not introduced by this PR)

While `~/Windows` stays empty, Dockur sets it back to `2777` on each container start that reaches its Samba setup. The protected bind anchor under `/var/lib/omarchy/windows/mounts/users/<uid>/` has `0711`/`0755` parents and shares the directory's inode. Any local account can therefore list, create, delete or rename entries through that path, whatever the mode of `$HOME`. Guest-created files are forced to `0666` ([`samba.sh` L231-240](https://github.com/dockur/windows/blob/1e99833c8f7946238566ecd0d5d2b40ba5f6c03a/src/samba.sh#L231-L240)). The anchor route stays open through `stop` until the next privileged launch or remove, or until a reboot drops the bind. The `2777` mode itself survives reboot, so `~/Windows` stays reachable wherever `$HOME` lets other accounts through.

```text
               first Dockur start      next launch/remove              later starts (share still empty)
base           2777, open to others    2700, fails closed              blocked until chmod g-s
this PR        2777, open to others    700, succeeds                   2777 again each start
```

**Impact:** source-traced, not run. This PR neither creates nor widens the exposure, but it no longer ends in a failure. Between a start and the next privileged hardening, the manual's statement that other accounts "cannot browse their contents" does not hold.

**Suggested change:** not required for this PR's fix. This overlaps with open [#9783](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/9783), which changes the same two `chmod` lines and adds re-hardening after the guest reports ready and on stop (not reviewed here). Only one of the two needs to land.

**Test scope:** Source review of the current head, base and earlier reviewed head of `bin/omarchy-windows-vm` and its tests, Dockur `dockur/windows` source (`1e99833`), and gnulib `modechange.c`. Sandboxed runs (GNU coreutils 9.11, synthetic identity stubs) covered the chmod mode comparison, `prepare_user_mount_sources` with setgid and plain homes, the launcher test, and the compose test on the head and on the base. Diagnostic mutants reverted each `chmod` and the root-branch hardening call. Not run: the full install, launch and remove flows (Docker, root, `/dev/kvm`), the root-path mount-boundary test, and Samba itself.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
